text: Tokenization and pseudonymization both substitute a sensitive value for something else, but they're reversible in completely different ways, and confusing them with each other, or with anonymization, has real legal consequences.

Tokenization replaces a sensitive value with a token that has no mathematical relationship to the original. A credit card number becomes something like TOK-9f3e2a71, and you cannot derive the original through any computation, the only way back is a lookup in a separate, tightly controlled token vault. That's different from encryption, where the ciphertext still mathematically encodes the original. A token traveling through logs and third-party integrations has effectively zero value to anyone who intercepts it, because there's nothing to crack.

Pseudonymization replaces identifiers with a consistent substitute according to a defined method, while keeping a separate mapping that can reverse it. Customer 48213 might consistently become Patient-X92 throughout a research dataset, letting analysts see that the same patient shows up five times across tables without seeing who they really are. GDPR treats pseudonymized data as still personal data, because it's reversible with the mapping, but recognizes it as a risk-reducing safeguard precisely because reversal requires a separate, protectable table.

Anonymization is the one that actually removes the ability to re-identify someone, done correctly, there's no mapping to reverse at all, which is why genuinely anonymized data generally falls outside GDPR entirely. If you can get back to the original value by any legitimate path, it's pseudonymization, not anonymization, no matter how the substitute looks. And both tokenization and pseudonymization only hold up if the vault or mapping table is protected as rigorously as the data it stands in for.

An unsecured vault or an unprotected mapping spreadsheet provides no real protection, it just relocates the sensitive data somewhere that now also needs defending. Next up: encryption, the technique both of these get compared against.
